chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad altogether, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ziyad al-Qandi, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Acquire a riding animal, for indeed it is an adornment, and needs are fulfilled upon it, and its sustenance is upon God, Majestic is His mention.'
He said: 'And Ammar ibn al-Mubarak narrated the same to me and added to it: and upon it you meet your brethren.'
And it is reported that he said: 'How wondrous is the owner of the riding animal — how could any need escape him?'

key_terms.الحوائج: Needs, necessities — including errands, travel for commerce, visiting kin, attending to affairs
key_terms.الدابة: A riding animal, typically a horse, donkey, or mule used for transport and carrying loads
key_terms.جل ذكره: Majestic is His mention — an honorific formula used with God's name
key_terms.رزقها على الله: Its sustenance is upon God — the animal's food and upkeep are guaranteed by divine provision
key_terms.زين: Adornment, distinction, prestige — keeping a fine animal was a mark of social status in Arab culture

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the benefits of keeping a riding animal?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) encourages the acquisition of riding animals, highlighting three benefits: it is a source of dignity and social status, it facilitates meeting one's needs, and its sustenance is guaranteed by God. A supplementary narration from Ammar ibn al-Mubarak adds a fourth benefit: a riding animal enables one to visit and maintain ties with one's brothers in faith. The hadith reflects the practical realities of 2nd century Arabia, where a riding animal was essential for travel, commerce, and social interaction. The rhetorical exclamation at the end — 'How wondrous is it that a person who owns a riding animal could ever miss having their needs fulfilled' — emphasizes the comprehensiveness of this blessing.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, and a number of our companions, from sahl Bin Ziyad, altogether from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ziyad Al qindy, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>: ‘Take the animal, for it is an adornment, and fulfil the needs upon it, and its sustenance is upon Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Majestic is His<sup>azwj</sup> Mention’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘And it was narrated with to me by Ammar Bin Al Mubarak, and there was an increase in it, 
‘(He<sup>asws</sup> said): ‘And meet your brethren (by riding) upon it’.
And it is reported that, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> wonder at the owner of the animal how he would miss the (fulfilment of) needs’.
en.sarwar: 9. Ali ibn Ibrahim a number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad all from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ziyad al-Qandiy from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following:
“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘You must have a stumper; it is of beautification and helps meet one’s needs and its sustenance is with Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious.’
He (the narrator) has said that narrated to me ‘Ammar ibn al-Mubarak with the addition of ‘and ride it to meet your brothers (in belief).’
It is also narrated that he (the Imam) said, ‘How can one who has a stumper miss fulfilling his needs?”’
